assessment: The observations establish uneven access, late or missed sessions, booking conflicts, and variable administration time. They do not establish whether spare room-hours coincide with usable rehearsal opportunities. The following capability is speculative; eight-week success and administrative feasibility remain unproven.

openings.claim: A hypothetical ensemble-aware booking broker could detect when two differently named groups depend on the same indispensable musician and propose confirmed exchanges that make both rehearsals attendable. Its presently testable partial capability is identifying group pairs that cannot actually rehearse simultaneously.
openings.delta: Extend the booking unit from a group name to its minimum viable attendance conditions. A room vacancy alone would no longer count as a usable alternative. Full operation would require accurate attendance constraints, acceptable windows, equipment requirements, exchange consent, and one authoritative booking record.
openings.prediction: If indispensable shared membership contributes to unusable bookings, contacts will identify specific overlapping reservations that could not both proceed with the required players; these should correspond to documented late or missed sessions more often than comparable reservations without such overlap. No identified overlap would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Use short telephone or in-person conversations with the twelve contacts to request group-pair incompatibilities and retrospective reasons for the fourteen late or missed sessions; personal musician names are unnecessary. Compare those reports with the existing calendars. On paper, attempt one mutually acceptable exchange for an identified pair, checking equipment and windows. Record conversation and scheduling minutes. This tests detection and exchange feasibility; it does not establish the eight-week outcome.
assumptions: Shared indispensable players exist and contacts can report incompatibilities accurately; neither is established.
Any enacted exchange preserves every requesting group’s weekly 60-minute access, the two performances, existing equipment, fees, rooms, and staffed hours.
Changes require confirmation through telephone or in-person channels and a synchronized authoritative record.
The full capability would need to reduce other administration enough to average at most two hours weekly; that dependency must be measured rather than assumed.
